actions.action: Add a keyboard-accessible “Move to position” control.
actions.mechanism: A numbered destination lets users relocate an item directly without dragging or repeated movement commands.
actions.implementation: Open a labeled form from each item; accept positions 1–40. On confirmation, reorder existing IDs, record undo, and restore item focus.
actions.check: Using only keyboard input, move item 37 to position 2; undo restores the exact previous ID sequence.
actions.risk: Explain that the number denotes the final position.

actions.action: Offer an explicit keyboard move mode.
actions.mechanism: Directional commands support incremental placement while keeping ordinary list navigation separate from reordering.
actions.implementation: Activate “Reorder” with Enter; use arrows to move and Home/End for boundaries. Enter commits one undoable move; Escape cancels. Announce position.
actions.check: Without a pointer, move an item through several positions, cancel, then repeat and commit; undo restores its starting position.
actions.risk: Scope shortcuts to move mode; test screen-reader interaction.

actions.action: Retain an accessible, page-lifetime undo history.
actions.mechanism: Saved ID sequences make every committed move reversible, rather than relying on a temporary notification.
actions.implementation: Before each move, push the ordered IDs onto an uncapped page-lifetime stack. Provide a persistent keyboard-focusable Undo button; restore order without regenerating IDs.
actions.check: Perform 50 moves, wait, then undo all 50. Every intermediate order must match its snapshot and retain all 40 IDs.
actions.risk: If items can be deleted, define restoration behavior explicitly.
